title: What changed in Rust 1.80 → 1.98 and edition 2024

recipes.name: Move si-solver to edition 2024: cargo fix rewrites 10 #[no_mangle], hand-fix 7 static_mut_refs
recipes.what: On 1.98.1, `cargo fix --edition` on a copy of solver/ changed only the 10 `#[no_mangle]` exports to `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]`, left `edition = "2021"` in Cargo.toml, and left 7 `static_mut_refs` sites that fail the build once the edition is 2024; neither rewrite changed a byte of the wasm (measured).
recipes.how: 1) `cargo +1.98.1 fix --edition --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (needs a clean git tree or --allow-dirty): it rewrites 3 attributes in lib.rs and 7 in rapier_law.rs and prints the 7 static_mut_refs warnings it cannot fix. `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` compiles warning-free on edition 2021 since 1.82, so this step can land on its own. 2) Set `edition = "2024"` by hand. 3) Rewrite the 7 sites without moving any line: lib.rs:28/33 and rapier_law.rs:78 `unsafe { X.as_mut_ptr() }` -> `(&raw mut X).cast::<f64>()` (taking `&raw` of a static mut is safe since 1.82, no unsafe block); lib.rs:183/184 `&mut BODIES` / `&COLLIDERS` -> `&mut *(&raw mut BODIES)` / `&*(&raw const COLLIDERS)`; rapier_law.rs:738/743 `SOLVER.snapshot.as_ptr()` / `.len()` -> `(*(&raw const SOLVER)).snapshot.as_ptr()` / `.len()`. Whether those references are sound is the unsafe-ffi lane's question; this recipe states what the compiler now demands (checked: a solver-shaped module written this way builds warning-free under 2024, imports nothing, and its step and snapshot exports work). 4) Rebuild through build.mjs and compare the digest.
recipes.gotchas: Under 2024 static_mut_refs is a deny-by-default lint, not a hard error: the compiler reports `#[deny(static_mut_refs)]` (part of rust_2024_compatibility) and `#![allow(static_mut_refs)]` makes the crate build (checked), so an allow is a wrong fix that still compiles. There is no automatic migration for it. Explicit `&X` / `&mut X`, `ref` bindings and autoref method calls such as `.as_mut_ptr()`, `.as_ptr()` and `.len()` are flagged; by-value indexing such as `BODIES[base + k]` and `HEIGHTS[i]` is not (checked). Byte identity holds only while panicking code keeps its line: the module embeds panic locations, and a blank line inserted at the top of rapier_law.rs changed 22 bytes (digest b03c2b70...) while the same shift in lib.rs changed none (measured), so a reflow by `cargo fmt` under style_edition 2024 can move the digest without changing behaviour. Identity was measured on the Windows host (sha256 b21c7f15... for 2021, for 2024 with the lint allowed, and for 2024 with the &raw rewrite), not against the Linux pin.
recipes.engine_note: The 10 attribute sites are the exports in solver/src/lib.rs (bodies_ptr, colliders_ptr, step) and solver/src/rapier_law.rs (heights_ptr, canon_zero, solver_load, solver_step, snapshot_ptr, snapshot_len, solver_clear_warmstart); the 7 static_mut_refs sites are lib.rs:28, 33, 183, 184 and rapier_law.rs:78, 738, 743 in the local checkout. A line-preserving migration should leave fixtures/solver.sha256 unchanged; write T2's restore exports in the 2024 spelling from the start. The dependencies are already edition-2024 crates (rapier3d-f64 0.35.3: edition 2024, rust-version 1.86; nalgebra 0.35.0: edition 2024, rust-version 1.89.0) and editions are per crate, so the solver's own edition changes nothing inside them.

recipes.name: Expect edition 2024 to drop if-let scrutinee and tail-expression temporaries earlier
recipes.what: Edition 2024 drops the temporaries of an `if let` scrutinee before the `else` branch runs and drops a block's tail-expression temporaries before its local variables; both reorder `Drop` side effects (checked), and the first is why let chains (stable 1.88) are 2024-only.
recipes.how: Rules: in `if let P = e { .. } else { .. }` the temporaries of `e` now drop before `else` (2021: after the whole expression); in a tail expression they now drop before the block's locals (2021: after), so `c.borrow().len()` as the tail of the block that owns `c` compiles (E0597 in 2021). Migration: `if_let_rescope` is auto-fixed by rewriting to `match`, which keeps the 2021 order, so review each rewrite; `tail_expr_drop_order` only warns. After the switch write `if let Some(x) = a && let Ok(y) = f(x) { .. }` instead of nested if-lets. `if let` guards in match arms (`Some(s) if let Some(x) = parse(s) =>`, 1.95) are not tied to the edition: they compile in 2021 as well (checked).
recipes.rust_version: edition 2024 (1.85+); let chains 1.88 (2024 only); if-let guards 1.95 (every edition)
recipes.gotchas: The automatic `match` rewrite preserves the old, later drop, so the deadlock the edition fixes (a RwLock read guard kept alive into an `else` that takes the write lock) survives the migration unless the rewrite is undone on purpose. In 2021 a let chain is the error 'let chains are only allowed in Rust 2024 or later' (checked). Tail-expression temporaries are also sometimes no longer extended to the enclosing scope, so a borrow that compiled through extension in 2021 can fail in 2024. 1.91 applied the 2024 if-let rule to temporaries made by pin!, format_args!, write! and writeln! in 2024 scrutinees.
recipes.engine_note: cargo fix --edition on the solver copy reported no if_let_rescope or tail_expr_drop_order site (measured): `ensure()` in rapier_law.rs uses `if let Some(loaded) = solver.loaded.as_ref()` with no else, and the other matches are let-else. The rules start to matter in the planned host bindings (Godot, then Unreal), where a wrapper may hold a lock guard or RefCell borrow over the solver's static state across an if-let.

recipes.name: Know which edition-2024 changes cargo fix --edition migrates and which stay manual
recipes.what: Of the Edition Guide's 2024 list, `cargo fix --edition` rewrites unsafe attributes, unsafe extern blocks, unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn, if-let (into match), RPIT over-capture (inserts `use<..>`), `expr` -> `expr_2021`, `gen` -> `r#gen`, `Box<[T]>::into_iter`, prelude collisions, reserved `#".."#` syntax, match-ergonomics patterns, `env::set_var` calls and Cargo.toml key names; it does not migrate static_mut_refs, tail-expression drop order, never-type fallback, missing macro fragment specifiers, combined doctests or the resolver change.
recipes.how: Run `cargo fix --edition` once per target and feature set that compiles distinct code (it only sees what that configuration compiles), read everything it prints, flip `edition = "2024"` by hand, then build, test and `cargo fmt`. What changes meaning: `expr` fragments now also match `const { .. }` and `_`; `-> impl Trait` captures every in-scope lifetime (narrow with `+ use<..>`, available in all editions since 1.82); `Box<[T]>::into_iter()` yields `T`, not `&T`; never-type fallback is `!`, not `()`; `extern` blocks must be `unsafe extern` with per-item `safe` / `unsafe`; unsafe operations inside an `unsafe fn` need their own `unsafe {}` (a warning); `std::env::set_var` / `remove_var` are unsafe; `gen` is reserved; `Future` / `IntoFuture` join the prelude; resolver "3" is implied; doctests are combined into one binary (opt out per test with `standalone_crate`); rustfmt's style edition follows the edition unless `style_edition` is configured separately.
recipes.gotchas: Doctests, macros and build-time generated code are not migrated. The expr_2021 rewrite exists to keep old macro matching; undoing it changes which arm matches (checked: a `const { .. }` argument picks the `$e:expr` arm in 2024 and the `const $b:block` arm in 2021). impl_trait_overcaptures cannot always fix argument-position impl Trait. Code that relied on `()` never-type fallback already fails in 2021 on 1.92+ through a deny lint and is a type error (E0277) in 2024. Doctests that assert panic Location lines or type_name output can break once doctests are combined.
recipes.engine_note: The solver has no extern blocks, unsafe fns, macros, RPIT returns, `gen` identifiers or boxed slices, so of this list only the unsafe attributes touch it (measured: cargo fix changed nothing else). The rustfmt style edition is the one item that can move the digest with no semantic change, because a reformat shifts panic-location line numbers (see the solver migration recipe).

recipes.name: Treat wasm32-unknown-unknown's six default features as byte changes, and -relaxed-simd as no ban
recipes.what: On 1.98.1 wasm32-unknown-unknown enables sign-ext and mutable-globals (in codegen since 1.70), multivalue and reference-types (default since 1.82, LLVM 19) and bulk-memory and nontrapping-fptoint (since 1.87, LLVM 20); simd128 and relaxed-simd are off. None of the six is float arithmetic: `f64 as i32` saturates the same with nontrapping-fptoint and bulk-memory switched off (checked), while every change to the default set changes module bytes. `-C target-feature=-relaxed-simd` leaves the default set as it is and does not stop a function that enables relaxed-simd itself.
recipes.how: Read the set with `rustc +1.98.1 --print cfg --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` or `cfg!(target_feature = "...")`, and read what a built module used from its `target_features` custom section (the solver copy lists +bulk-memory, +bulk-memory-opt, +call-indirect-overlong, +multivalue, +mutable-globals, +nontrapping-fptoint, +reference-types, +sign-ext). For an MVP-only module on stable use wasm32v1-none (Tier 2 since 1.84; no std, only core and alloc; only mutable-globals); turning features off on wasm32-unknown-unknown does not rebuild the precompiled std, and a full MVP build needs nightly -Zbuild-std. Keep the -relaxed-simd pin in .cargo/config.toml and build.mjs, and add a cheap gate that the module's target_features section lists neither +relaxed-simd nor +simd128, beside T3's opcode lint.
recipes.rust_version: 1.70 (sign-ext, mutable-globals), 1.82 (multivalue, reference-types), 1.84 (wasm32v1-none Tier 2), 1.87 (bulk-memory, nontrapping-fptoint); measured on 1.98.1
recipes.gotchas: reference-types (1.82) changed call_indirect's table immediate to an over-long 5-byte LEB (the +call-indirect-overlong entry), which decoders without reference-types support reject. Enabling multivalue did not change the extern "C" ABI. The relaxed-SIMD intrinsics (e.g. core::arch::wasm32::f64x2_relaxed_madd) are stable since 1.82: a `#[target_feature(enable = "simd128,relaxed-simd")]` function compiles under `-C target-feature=-relaxed-simd` (checked) and, in the scratch probe, emitted f64x2.relaxed_madd, recorded +relaxed-simd in target_features, and returned the fused result under node 22 on this x86 host (-8.67e-19 where a separate multiply and add give 0). On wasm such a function is callable without an unsafe block. Switching bulk-memory and nontrapping-fptoint off changed the probe's size (1591014 -> 1591189 bytes) but not its results.
recipes.engine_note: solver/.cargo/config.toml and solver/build.mjs both pass -C target-feature=-relaxed-simd; on 1.98.1 that flag changes nothing in the default set (checked), so it guards against a future default, while FLAGS.md's 'this build disables' does not cover a dependency function that opts in with #[target_feature] - only inspecting the module (T3's opcode lint, or the target_features section) catches that. A toolchain bump that changes the default set, as 1.82 and 1.87 did, changes the digest in fixtures/solver.sha256; the golden hash should not move for that reason.

recipes.name: Expect wasm32 undefined symbols to fail the link since 1.96 and the standard C ABI since 1.89
recipes.what: Since 1.96 rustc no longer passes --allow-undefined to wasm-ld, so an extern function with no definition is a link error ('undefined symbol') instead of a silent `env` import; since 1.89 `extern "C"` on wasm32-unknown-unknown follows the standard tool-conventions C ABI, which changed how aggregates are passed and left scalars alone; 1.84 removed the wasm32-wasi target name (now wasm32-wasip1) and added wasm32v1-none at Tier 2.
recipes.how: Declare each intended host import explicitly with `#[link(wasm_import_module = "env")]` (or another module name) on its `unsafe extern "C"` block; `-C link-arg=--allow-undefined` restores the old behaviour for a whole build. Keep exports scalar and pointer only (u32, f64, *const u8), which both ABIs lower the same way; a #[repr(C)] struct passed by value is passed indirectly under the 1.89+ ABI where the legacy ABI split it into separate parameters. Name WASI targets wasm32-wasip1 or wasm32-wasip2.
recipes.rust_version: 1.84 (wasm32-wasi removed, wasm32v1-none Tier 2), 1.89 (standard C ABI), 1.96 (no --allow-undefined); measured on 1.98.1
recipes.gotchas: Before 1.96 a misspelt or missing extern fn produced a module importing `env.<name>`, which a loader that instantiates with no import object discovered only at instantiation. 1.86 made the wasm_c_abi future-compatibility warning a hard error (it concerned wasm-bindgen older than 0.2.89). 1.91.0 broke #[link(wasm_import_module)] across crates (same-named imports from different modules could resolve to the wrong function); 1.91.1 fixed it.
recipes.engine_note: The solver declares no extern block and imports nothing (build.mjs instantiates with `new WebAssembly.Instance(module)` and no import object), so on 1.96+ an accidental undefined symbol fails `cargo build` instead of the JS instantiation. Its ten exports take u32/f64 and return u32/f64/pointers, the class the C ABI post says is unaffected. Keep T3's no-imports check as a second gate, and give T2's restore exports the same scalar/pointer signatures.

recipes.name: Replace flat-buffer index math with 1.86-1.93 std APIs: as_chunks_mut, get_disjoint_mut, as_array
recipes.what: Stable std now covers what the solver does by hand: `<[T]>::as_chunks_mut::<N>()` (1.88) views a flat f64 buffer as `[[f64; N]]`, `get_disjoint_mut([i, j])` (1.86) hands out two records mutably and reports overlap as an `Err`, `<[T]>::as_array::<N>()` (1.93) turns a sub-slice into `&[T; N]`, `strict_add` and the other `strict_*` methods (1.91) panic on overflow even with overflow-checks off, `f64::midpoint` (1.85) and `next_up` / `next_down` (1.86) avoid overflow and epsilon tricks, `cfg_select!` (1.95) replaces cfg-if, and `floor` / `round` / `trunc` (const since 1.90) and `mul_add` (const since 1.94) work in constants.
recipes.how: Write `let (records, rest) = buf.as_chunks_mut::<BODY_STRIDE>(); debug_assert!(rest.is_empty());` and index `records[i][HX]`; take a pair with `let [a, b] = records.get_disjoint_mut([i, j])?;`; take a quaternion as `b[6..10].as_array::<4>()`; use `strict_*` where overflow is a bug (counts, offsets) and keep `wrapping_*` where wrap-around is intended (hash mixing); use `cfg_select!` for wasm-versus-native constants. Keep midpoint and mul_add out of law arithmetic: the law must repeat the JS kernel's exact operation sequence.
recipes.rust_version: 1.85-1.95 as listed per API; all present on the 1.98.1 pin
recipes.gotchas: `strict_*` ignores `overflow-checks = false` (checked: exit 101 under -C overflow-checks=off), so in the solver's panic = "abort" wasm build it becomes a trap; use it only where aborting is right. `get_disjoint_mut` also returns Err for an out-of-bounds index, and `as_chunks_mut` returns a remainder that must be checked. APIs newer than rust-toolchain.toml's pin fail to compile. Other additions in the period: LazyCell / LazyLock (1.80), Vec::extract_if (1.87), array_windows (1.94), Box::new_zeroed (1.92), core::hint::cold_path (1.95), assert_matches! (1.96, not in the prelude).
recipes.engine_note: lib.rs `body_at` / `field` and `resolve_pair(bodies, i, j)` (two bodies mutated through index arithmetic), rapier_law.rs `body_at` / `collider_at` copy loops and `quat_from_body(&b)` are the index-arithmetic sites; `mix_u64`'s wrapping_mul / wrapping_add must stay wrapping. Any such rewrite changes the digest (code and panic locations move) but should leave the golden hash unchanged; prove that with the three-engine golden run.

recipes.name: Keep 1.98's f64::algebraic_* methods out of the law: the std docs allow different results per run
recipes.what: 1.98 stabilized `algebraic_add`, `_sub`, `_mul`, `_div` and `_rem` on f32 and f64, which let the compiler combine and reorder operations, swap division for reciprocal multiplication and ignore the sign of zero; the core docs say the same inputs may produce different results even within one program run. They compile on stable with no feature gate and no warning (checked).
recipes.how: Keep the law to + - * / and sqrt, as lib.rs's header comment says, and keep algebraic_* (and mul_add) out of solver/src by review plus a CI grep for `algebraic_`. Constants may be computed by const fn since 1.82: `const SLIDE_ANGLE: f64 = radians(50.0)` has the same bits as the runtime call for this non-NaN expression (checked). Never hash a NaN's bits: f64::NAN is guaranteed quiet since 1.88, but its payload and sign may change across Rust versions and targets, and a NaN produced at compile time need not match the one produced at run time - reject or canonicalize first.
recipes.rust_version: algebraic_* 1.98; const-fn float arithmetic 1.82; NAN quiet guarantee 1.88
recipes.gotchas: A model trained before 1.98 calls these nightly-only; on 1.98.1 they are plain stable methods and nothing in rustc warns about them. The 1.82 announcement warns that `(0.0 / 0.0).is_sign_positive()` can differ between compile time and run time and across hardware, optimization level and surrounding code, and advises fully portable code to avoid to_bits and to test `f.signum() == 1.0` rather than `f.is_sign_positive()` (the advice concerns NaN results). No `algebraic_` appears in the pinned rapier3d-f64 0.35.3, parry3d-f64 0.30.2, nalgebra 0.35.0, simba 0.10.2, glam 0.33.10 or libm 0.2.16 sources (grep of the local cargo registry), so a dependency bump is where they could enter.
recipes.engine_note: rapier_law.rs computes CLIMB_ANGLE and SLIDE_ANGLE as consts; `bad` rejects NaN before `mix_f64` hashes `to_bits()`, and `canon_zero` passes NaN through untouched - the discipline the NaN notes require. Add `algebraic_` to the source lints that accompany T3's relaxed-SIMD opcode lint, and grep the Cargo.lock diff's crates for it on every dependency bump.

recipes.name: Stop sorting floats with partial_cmp().unwrap_or(Equal): 1.81+ sorts panic on a non-total order
recipes.what: 1.81 replaced the slice sorts with driftsort (stable) and ipnsort (unstable), which may panic when the comparison is not a total order; the old 'NaN-tolerant' idiom `sort_by(|a, b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap_or(Ordering::Equal))` panics on 1.98.1 with 'user-provided comparison function does not correctly implement a total order' once a NaN is in a 64-element slice (checked), where older sorts silently returned some order.
recipes.how: Sort f64 keys with `total_cmp` (`v.sort_by(|a, b| a.total_cmp(b))`), which puts -0.0 before 0.0 and a positive NaN last (checked); better, reject NaN before sorting and sort by integer keys where they exist; keep PartialOrd and Ord consistent; never depend on which of several equal elements binary_search returns (1.82 changed it).
recipes.rust_version: 1.81+ (new sorts); binary_search change 1.82; BTreeMap::append 1.96; derive(PartialOrd) fast path 1.98
recipes.gotchas: The release note says 'may panic': detection is best-effort - a comparator that never returns Equal did not panic on a 200-element probe, so a passing test proves nothing. In the solver's panic = "abort" wasm build a sort panic is a trap. 1.96 made BTreeMap::append able to panic on incorrect Ord impls, and 1.98's derive(PartialOrd) fast path breaks types whose PartialOrd and Ord disagree.
recipes.engine_note: rapier_law.rs `rebuild_snapshot` sorts contact pairs by `(collider1.into_raw_parts(), collider2.into_raw_parts())` - integer tuples, a total order, safe. Future sorts by f64 (T6 reachability sweep, T5 replay corpus ordering) should use total_cmp or integer keys, after NaN rejection.

recipes.name: Expect 1.86-1.98 lint escalations to break old unsafe and macro code on a toolchain bump
recipes.what: Lints tightened in the period, in every edition: dangerous_implicit_autorefs (added 1.88, deny 1.89), missing_fragment_specifier (hard error 1.89), semicolon_in_expressions_from_macros (deny 1.91), never_type_fallback_flowing_into_unsafe and dependency_on_unit_never_type_fallback (deny 1.92), deref_nullptr (deny 1.93), invalid_runtime_symbol_definitions (new, deny 1.98); new warn-by-default lints include missing_abi (1.86), mismatched_lifetime_syntaxes (1.89), dangling_pointers_from_locals (1.91) and linker_messages (1.97, outside the `warnings` group).
recipes.how: Treat each toolchain bump as a lint audit: build with the new pin and read every new warning and error. Write `&mut *ptr` / `&*ptr` explicitly before indexing or calling methods through a raw pointer; annotate `f::<()>()?` where code relied on `()` never-type fallback; always spell `extern "C"`; no trailing `;` in a macro used as an expression; never define `memcmp` / `memset` / `strlen`-named symbols with another signature (no_std wasm crates sometimes do); never return a pointer to a local.
recipes.rust_version: per lint as listed (1.86-1.98); measured on 1.98.1
recipes.gotchas: The never-type lints fire only when the affected crate itself is built (1.92 announcement), so a dependency with the pattern keeps building while a copied snippet fails. linker_messages is not affected by the warnings lint group (1.97 announcement). The wasm_c_abi future-compatibility warning became a hard error in 1.86.
recipes.engine_note: On 1.98.1 the solver builds with its 7 static_mut_refs warnings and no other lint (measured), and rapier_law.rs's `unsafe { &mut *core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(SOLVER) }` is already the explicit form these lints accept. Build the next bump with CARGO_BUILD_WARNINGS=deny (see the Cargo recipe) so a newly escalated lint stops CI instead of scrolling past.

recipes.name: Gate solver CI with Cargo's build.warnings (1.97), not RUSTFLAGS, and keep --locked across resolver 3
recipes.what: Cargo 1.80-1.98 added knobs the solver build should use: `build.warnings` / CARGO_BUILD_WARNINGS (1.97) denies local lint warnings without touching RUSTFLAGS; resolver "3" (1.84, implied by edition 2024) makes resolution MSRV-aware; check-cfg is always on (1.80); and cargo info (1.82), automatic cache GC (1.88), cargo fix using the build commands' target selection (1.89), publish --workspace (1.90), build.build-dir and `--target host-tuple` (1.91), config `include` and TOML 1.1 manifests (1.94) and resolver.lockfile-path (1.97).
recipes.how: In CI run the solver build as `CARGO_BUILD_WARNINGS=deny node solver/build.mjs --check` (or set `[build] warnings = "deny"` in solver/.cargo/config.toml). RUSTFLAGS outranks every config rustflags entry (order: CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS, RUSTFLAGS, target.<triple>/<cfg>.rustflags, build.rustflags), so a -Dwarnings placed in config is dropped whenever build.mjs sets RUSTFLAGS, while build.warnings is not a rustflag (measured: with build.mjs's RUSTFLAGS it failed the edition-2021 copy on its 7 warnings: 'warnings are denied by `build.warnings` configuration'). Keep building with --locked so an edition bump's resolver 3 cannot move Cargo.lock (measured: the edition-2024 copy built with --locked --offline and an unchanged lock). Declare any custom cfg in `[lints.rust] unexpected_cfgs` check-cfg so the 1.80 lint stays quiet.
recipes.rust_version: Cargo 1.80-1.98 per knob as listed; measured with cargo 1.98.1
recipes.gotchas: build.warnings covers only lint warnings from local packages, not dependency or non-lint warnings. Config `include` accepts only paths ending in .toml. Automatic GC deletes downloaded crates unused for about three months and does not run under --offline or --frozen, so an offline rebuild of an old commit may need a fetch first. TOML 1.1 syntax in Cargo.toml raises the development MSRV (Cargo parses TOML 1.1 from 1.94), though published manifests stay readable by older parsers. With incompatible-rust-versions = "fallback" the resolver only prefers compatible versions; with none available it still picks one.
recipes.engine_note: solver/Cargo.toml (edition 2021, so resolver 2), solver/.cargo/config.toml (target rustflags that build.mjs's RUSTFLAGS replaces - the reason build.mjs repeats -relaxed-simd), solver/build.mjs, and the digest job in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
